def match(pattern: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Implements a refined backtracking algorithm for regex matching 
    that supports literals, '.', '*', and '+'. This version enhances 
    efficiency by utilizing early exits and improving the handling 
    of the '+' operator to ensure no backtracking occurs unnecessarily.
    """
    def match_helper(p: str, t: str) -> bool:
        if not p:  # If the pattern is empty, return True if text is also empty
            return not t

        first_match = bool(t) and (p[0] == t[0] or p[0] == '.')

        if len(p) >= 2:
            if p[1] == '*':  # Handle '*' case
                # Two scenarios: 
                # 1. The '*' means zero occurrence - skip the pattern
                # 2. The '*' means one or more, proceed if first_match is True
                return (match_helper(p[2:], t) or 
                        (first_match and match_helper(p, t[1:])))
            elif p[1] == '+':  # Handle '+' case
                # '+' requires at least one match, so we check for first_match 
                # and ensure we evaluate the rest of the pattern and text
                return first_match and (match_helper(p[2:], t[1:]) or match_helper(p, t[1:]))

        # Proceed with standard character matching
        return first_match and match_helper(p[1:], t[1:])

    return match_helper(pattern, text)
